note: Example data: an invented online store for hiking and camping gear, with invented accounts, not a real business. Every number in expected_output.json follows from this input.
request: Hey Claude, I just added the "marketing-mix-model-builder" skill. Build a marketing mix model for our store from the last two and a half years, tell me what each channel really returns, and how to split the same budget. We ran a Meta geo lift test in March.
business: Example Trail Supply, an online store for hiking and camping gear (invented example)
outcome: weekly store revenue, net of refunds, all orders from every source (Shopify)

sources.from: Shopify connector: get_orders_count for the window, then get_orders walked page by page until has_more was false, checked against that count, test and cancelled orders dropped, summed by week

sources.data: Google Search (non-brand), Google Performance Max, Google Search (brand)
sources.from: Google Ads connector, gaql by segments.week (spend and impressions), split by campaign type and brand campaign names
Meta connector, get_insights_adaccount with time_increment 7 (spend and impressions)
TikTok connector, integrated_report_basic by day in 30-day chunks (spend and impressions), summed by week; no spend before 2025-06-23
Pinterest connector for the last 12 weeks (the API keeps 90 days); the user's Pinterest Ads export of weekly spend and impressions for the 118 weeks before

lift_tests.type: geo holdout (Meta ads off in 30% of US regions)
